findings.summary: The real drain detects the checks stage by matching a UI display string. Because the producer is sent back, the table says 'checks' while the producer is still running.
findings.evidence: StageWatch records InFlightStage::Checks whenever a UI line starts with "producer   ". producer.rs:191 prints that line after every producer invocation, not once when the producer phase ends. With PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS = 1 (run/mod.rs:1034), a failed self-check sends the producer back (line 291) and runs it again, so the row reads 'checks' during the second producer invocation. A timed-out or failed producer also prints the line, so its row briefly moves to 'checks'. The table exists so later crash-recovery jobs can act on the stage (producer retry vs. re-check), and a crash during a send-back would leave a misleading 'checks' row. The trigger is also fragile: rewording the display line silently stops the checks stage from being recorded. No test exercises the checks stage through RealSteps; only the stub calls stage(Checks) directly. A sounder fix: have the run pipeline report the stage itself, e.g. a stage callback passed into Athena::go, called where run/mod.rs starts the checks after producer.rs returns Flow::Go. Then add a RealSteps test that a send-back keeps the row at 'producer'.

findings.summary: The design doc and CHANGELOG say the row moves 'at each stage change', which the real steps get wrong in the send-back case above.
findings.evidence: The doc says 'moves it at each stage change'. With RealSteps the checks stage is recorded after any producer invocation line, including ones followed by a send-back.

summary: The retry fixes the main problem from the last attempt. The real drain (RealSteps) now records the live work tree, `<state>/jobs/<id>/work`, through a `StateDir` helper that the producer also uses. Two tests that run through the real steps confirm it: the recorded path matches the directory the producer was given and is never the kept-work directory, including for a timed-out job. I ran the 7 new drain tests and the 11 state tests; all passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. All 8 acceptance criteria are met, and every changed file is on the expected deliverables list. The verdict is still fail because of one major soundness finding. The real drain marks a job as being at the checks stage when it sees a UI line starting with "producer   ". That line is printed after every producer attempt, and the producer gets one send-back, so the table can say "checks" while the producer is running again. Failed or timed-out producer attempts also move the row to "checks" briefly. Later crash-recovery jobs will decide what to do from this stage, so a wrong stage leads to the wrong recovery. The fix is to have the run pipeline report the stage itself, for example a stage callback passed into `Athena::go` and called where the checks begin. A test through the real steps should then show that a send-back keeps the row at "producer".
